fixture_provenance.methodology: Fresh private volumes per mode. Both modes install the same core extension, roles, publication, grants and one pgduck engine; only mirroring starts a subscription. One persistent application psql session. Two-second CPU/memory and publication observers run in both modes. Mirror progress uses published source XIDs in the local journal; there are no recurring Iceberg data scans. The bounded fresh-database experiment rejects source XID wrap. CPU is cgroup usage including container observer overhead; host/controller/storage CPU is excluded. RSS double counts shared pages; PSS apportions them. Memory samples include caches. Publication latency is an observed upper bound with sampling and query delay, not exact commit-to-Iceberg latency. All S3 activity under the fixture iceberg prefix is final mirror output; the local trace labels that prefix local_mirror. No intermediate capture logs exist. No global cache clearing or production acceptance threshold.
